claims.summary: Over any field, for finite nonempty X_nu in disjoint variable blocks and X their product, with degree the least degree of a representing polynomial: the least degree of a nonzero function supported in a product set prod A_nu is sum m_nu (m_nu the least degree of a nonzero function on X_nu supported in A_nu), and degree is additive on products of block functions (union of block Groebner bases, leading monomials multiply). Hence in the degree-D vanishing ideal of X, block-local errors of degree<=e with supports Z_nu have surviving common killers of degree k (k+e<=D) exactly when k>=sum m_nu for A_nu=X_nu minus Z_nu. A separating idempotent s with s w_i = w_i and s vanishing off the union U of supports (a span generator) equals 1_U on X, so 1-s has degree sum delta(1_A_nu), which on cubes can exceed sum m_nu by the factor b (errors at block origins of {0,1}^b: m=1, delta=b); a general idempotent protecting a 0/1-valued least killer p, s=1-p, costs sum m_nu where such a p exists (always over F_2; not over F_3 on {0,1,2}); protecting one point x_0 costs sum m_nu(x_0), the blocks' least degrees of functions supported in A_nu and nonzero at x_0, which can exceed sum m_nu. Degree additivity is the standard tensor fact, proved here for finite product sets.

claims.rationale: Gives the exact least surviving killer degree for block-local errors in domain models and shows the idempotent denominator pays the larger indicator degree.
